title: The Wreck of Cape Reckoning
premise: Theo Vane, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a disaster he may or may not have caused, takes a low-visibility job ferrying supplies to a survey expedition up the Reckoning River. When the team's radio goes silent, Theo is the only person positioned—and desperate enough—to go find them, discovering the expedition has uncovered evidence that could clear his name, evidence powerful people want buried. Hunted by a fixer named Corliss and betrayed by the one ally he trusted, Theo must lead the surviving expedition members across the range ahead of the snows. He reaches the pass with hours to spare, chooses to testify rather than vanish, and finally stops running.
about_author: Vesper Zhou is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons in remote mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He ferries supplies upriver for cash under a false name, establishing his exile and skill. A radio check from the survey camp comes through garbled, then not at all. Beat: restless unease—the life he built on movement feels thinner than usual.

chapters.title: Blacklist
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Theo's POV: the avalanche on the Kestrel Face, the inquiry, the two bans, the death he was blamed for. Present-day Theo decides checking on the silent camp is 'just due diligence.' Beat: guilt wearing the mask of pragmatism.

chapters.title: Empty Tents
chapters.summary: Theo arrives at the survey camp to find it stripped—equipment gone, blood on a tent pole, and a locked strongbox hidden under the cook's floor. Inside: geological surveys and documents naming a mining consortium. Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Theo tracks a trail into the forest and finds Ines Okafor, the expedition's geologist, wounded and hiding. She tells him the others were taken by men hired by the consortium, led by a fixer called Corliss. Beat: reluctant partnership; Theo wants to walk away and can't.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She explains the surveys prove the consortium falsified the reports that triggered the original Kestrel Face disaster—the same disaster that ruined Theo. Beat: Theo's exile reframed as theft; fury with nowhere to put it.

chapters.title: Corliss
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. The fixer reports to his employer that one witness remains unaccounted for, and learns Theo Vane's name—a man already discredited, easy to bury twice. Beat: cold menace; the hunt begins.

chapters.title: Downriver Men
chapters.summary: Theo and Ines evade a search party by taking the gorge route no guide uses. Theo's knowledge of the terrain saves them, but Ines sees how much of himself he's lost. Beat: trust forming in motion; first real conversation about what justice means when law failed you.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Him
chapters.summary: They reach the river town of Salt Landing, where Theo once lived under another name. An old friend, Marta, shelters them but warns that word of a reward has spread. Beat: belonging offered and refused; Theo almost stays.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Landing
chapters.summary: Marta's brother sells their location to Corliss's men for the reward. Theo gets Ines out through the fish market as the town burns behind them—Marta among the casualties. Beat: grief and rage; proof that stopping costs more.

chapters.title: The Range Ahead
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, planning chapter. The only escape is over the Serrano Pass, four days' climb, and the dry season ends in five. Ines can barely walk. He starts training her on the move. Beat: grim resolve; the mountain becomes both threat and home.

chapters.title: Cold Open
chapters.summary: First snow squall catches them early at the tree line. They shelter in a cave where Theo once guided tourists, and he tells Ines the truth about Kestrel Face—that he froze, that the report was partly true. Beat: confession; identity confronted honestly for the first time.

chapters.title: Ines's Evidence
chapters.summary: Ines reveals she kept duplicate core samples cached at a high station hut—physical proof beyond the papers. Getting it adds a day they don't have. Beat: hope that demands risk; Theo chooses the detour without being asked.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: A full whiteout on the glacier. Ines falls into a crevasse; Theo anchors and hauls her out, destroying his remaining rope and nearly himself. Beat: sacrifice made concrete; the guide who 'froze' holds.

chapters.title: Corliss Ascending
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. His men have found the samples' location from the burned town's informant and are moving up the pass behind them, better equipped, on radios. Beat: closing trap; the reader knows what Theo suspects.

chapters.title: The Hut
chapters.summary: They reach the station hut and recover the samples—but Corliss's advance man is waiting. Theo kills him in a close, ugly fight, his first. Beat: the cost of justice outside the law; Theo is no longer the man who ran.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Corliss's main party pins them at the col below the pass. Theo triggers a controlled avalanche using old survey charges, scattering the hunters but sealing the lower route. Beat: the mountain as weapon; mastery reclaimed.

chapters.title: Corliss Alone
chapters.summary: Corliss, having lost his men, climbs after them alone and catches them at the final ridge. In a brutal hand-to-hand struggle at the edge, Ines saves Theo's life, and Corliss falls. Beat: climax; violence answered, not celebrated.

chapters.title: The Pass
chapters.summary: Exhausted, frostbitten, they cross Serrano Pass hours before it closes for the season, the samples intact against Theo's chest. Beat: awe and emptiness; survival without yet knowing what it was for.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: The far side: green valley, a road, a town with telephones. Theo realizes he could disappear here forever with the proof—or use it. Ines tells him testimony would mean returning to face the inquiry that banned him. Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Two Countries
chapters.summary: Theo crosses back into the country that blacklisted him, deliberately, at a manned border post, giving his true name for the first time in years. Beat: surrender as strength; identity chosen rather than escaped.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: Hearing-room chapter, alternating Theo and Ines POVs. The samples and surveys break the consortium's case open; the Kestrel Face findings are overturned; Corliss's employer is indicted. Beat: justice inside the law at last, earned by everything done outside it.

chapters.title: Cape Reckoning
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Theo's POV. Cleared but changed, Theo declines the consortium's settlement and instead takes a post teaching mountain safety—stationary, rooted, at last. Ines writes from a new dig. Beat: belonging achieved; the man who kept moving finally stands still.
